findings.reason: entity.mjs:36 now calls decodeHTML. NAMED_RE (line 7) matches the whole `¬it;`. With entities ^4.4.0 (package.json:49), legacy-mode decoding turns the `&not` prefix into ¬, so `decoded !== match[0]` and line 37 emits a text_special token that consumes the whole match. This breaks the spec's rule that unknown names stay literal.
findings.claim: Swapping decodeHTMLStrict for decodeHTML makes invalid named references that start with a legacy entity name (e.g. ¬it;) decode partly (¬it;) instead of staying literal text as CommonMark requires.
findings.evidence: The diff replaces `decodeHTMLStrict(match[0])` with `decodeHTML(match[0])`. In entities ^4.4.0 (package.json:49), `decodeHTML` decodes in Legacy mode, which accepts semicolon-less legacy names like `&not`, `&copy` and `&amp` as a prefix. NAMED_RE `/^&([a-z][a-z0-9]{1,31});/i` matches the whole `¬it;`, and because `decoded !== match[0]` the rule emits a `text_special` token with the partly decoded content and consumes the whole match.

findings.reason: The diff changes only entity.mjs. A grep of test/ for &(not|copy|amp)<letters>; finds nothing, so the suite cannot catch the regression in C1/X1.
findings.claim: No test covers unknown entity names that begin with a legacy entity prefix.
findings.evidence: diff.patch changes only lib/rules_inline/entity.mjs and adds no fixtures. A search of test/ for inputs like `&not…;`, `&copy…;` or `&amp…;` with extra letters finds no matches.
